insert.symbols.equation.note: U:quill/equation: built on Slate's equation model, layout and galleries (core/slate/lib/equation*.mjs; the page is drawn by core/quill/lib/math-layout.mjs, OMML by core/quill/lib/omml.mjs); the tiles are drawn from MathML as in OneNote. Where Slate's rendering differs from wordcraft's: (1) Slate typesets with MathML in the browser and has no page, so the page view draws the equation itself from Slate's tree (core/quill/lib/math-layout.mjs: TeX-style boxes, a reduced spacing table, brackets as scaled glyphs where Word builds them from pieces); wordcraft lays out its own math tree (layout/src/math). (2) An equation is its linear text and is edited as text (the Edit Equation box); wordcraft edits a tree with a caret, so equation.type, move, backspace, delete and enter are not offered. (3) Slate has no inline or display, no m:jc and no OMML: those are Quill's (equation.display, equation.justify, core/quill/lib/omml.mjs); what Word wrote in a file is kept as it was until the equation is changed here. (4) The gallery is Office's nine built-in equations, not wordcraft's ten. (5) Number is not offered. Not checked against Word's own spacing. Ink Equation stays hidden: the app has no handwriting recogniser.

equation.tools.equation.note: U:quill/equation: the same built-in equations as Insert › Equation.

equation.tools.ink-equation.note: U:quill/equation: hidden. Ink Equation recognises handwriting with Microsoft's math input recogniser; the app has no handwriting engine. Type the equation in the linear format (or LaTeX with the LaTeX button) in the Edit Equation box.

equation.symbols.symbols.note: U:quill/equation: Slate's eight symbol sets; the tile row shows every set, the menu lists each set.

equation.structures.fraction.note: U:quill/equation: Slate's Fraction gallery (core/slate/lib/equation-catalog.mjs); a structure goes into the first empty slot of the equation being edited, or makes a new equation.

equation.equation-options.number.note: U:quill/equation: hidden. Equation numbering (a `#` field after the equation) is not translated; the app has no equation numbers.

equation.equation-options.display.note: U:quill/equation: Display puts the equation on a line of its own (m:oMathPara); Inline keeps it in the text (m:oMath).

equation.equation-options.justification.note: U:quill/equation: Left, Right, Centered and Centered as Group (m:jc) for a display equation.

equation.equation-options.close-equation.note: U:quill/equation: puts the caret after the equation.

equation.tools.convert.note: U:quill/equation: Professional shows the typeset equation, Linear its text as typed; Current is the selected equation, All every equation in the document.

equation.tools.normal-text.note: U:quill/equation: shows the equation as plain, non-math text (m:nor).

dialog.equation.note: U:quill/equation: replaced by editing the equation in place (the page view's editor and the Equation tab; equation.edit takes the text); Equation Options is the only equation box. The old Edit Equation box has no model, so nothing reaches it.

dialog.insertEquation.note: U:quill/equation: replaced by Insert New Equation putting an empty equation in the line, typed in place; the old Insert Equation box has no model, so nothing reaches it.
